title: Log2 on a Double returns the natural logarithm (known defect)
intent: Log2.kt:21 reads `else -> kotlin.math.ln(target.toDouble())`, so every non-Float input gets ln() instead of log2(). Log2(8.0) yields 2.0794415416798357 rather than 3.0. There IS a unit test - Log2Test.kt - and it passes, because its only non-Float fixtures are 0.0 and 1.0, the two arguments where log2, log10 and ln all agree. This case pins the wrong-but-current behaviour so the defect is recorded and the suite stays green; if someone fixes Log2 it goes red and the report says the defect looks fixed.

knownDefect.summary: Log2 applies ln() to every non-Float input, so Log2(8.0)=2.0794… not 3.0 and Log2(64.0)=4.1588… not 6.0
